# ShipFrame

> ShipFrame is an open-source AI coding workflow toolkit for teams that plan, prove and ship software changes with discipline. It turns natural-language development requests into a repeatable delivery lifecycle and works with Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode. Released under the MIT License.

ShipFrame provides reusable skills, agent workflows, templates and project profiles. The core lifecycle is: Refresh context → Discover requirements → Plan work → Implement → Verify → Review → Release evidence → PR/MR. It is built for teams that work from tickets, Git branches and pull/merge requests, and that require concrete release evidence before declaring work complete.

## Key facts

- **Name:** ShipFrame
- **What it is:** AI coding workflow toolkit / developer tool
- **Supported tools:** Claude Code (plugin-managed agents + hooks and /shipframe:<skill> commands), Codex CLI (/skills picker with $skill invocation and a routing table in AGENTS.md without changing user-owned config.toml), OpenCode (native skill discovery plus converted agents that inherit the global/default model unless overridden)
- **License:** MIT (free for personal and commercial use)
- **Platforms:** macOS, Linux
- **Repository:** https://github.com/juanitourquiza/shipframe
- **Landing page:** https://shipframe.hackeruna.com
- **Maintainer:** hackeruna — contact j@hackeruna.com
- **Optional memory:** integrates with Engram for persistent cross-session memory

## Install

Install once. Open `/skills`. Use ShipFrame workflows directly.

- One-line: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/juanitourquiza/shipframe/main/install.sh | bash`
- Homebrew: `brew tap juanitourquiza/shipframe && brew install shipframe && shipframe install --codex`
- Targets: `./install.sh --claude`, `--codex`, `--opencode`, or `--all`
- Safe checks and maintenance: `./install.sh --doctor --repo-only`, `./install.sh --repair --all`, `./install.sh --uninstall --all --yes`
- Native discovery, no lock-in: Claude plugin marketplace support with `/shipframe:code-review`, Codex CLI `/skills` then `$code-review`, and OpenCode native skill discovery after `shipframe install --opencode`.

## What's inside

- **Core workflow:** init-project, project-memory-refresh, feature-discovery, plan-expert, implement-task, code-review, create-task, create-issue, create-pr
- **Engineering discipline:** domain-modeling, codebase-design, tdd, bug-diagnosis, research, handoff
- **Release & evidence:** project-profile, project-release, release-checklist, frontend-release, backend-release, deploy-evidence
- **Integration & product:** mcp-debugging, client-copy-review, a11y-auditor (WCAG 2.2), design-expert, design-system-docs, design-system-setup
- **Knowledge wiki:** wiki-init, wiki-query, wiki-sync, wiki-forge
- **Project profiles:** generic core plus opt-in per-repo rules (release process, smoke-test routes, version policy, i18n, client copy). Starter packs for Angular, Laravel and MCP.

## Frequently asked questions

- **What is ShipFrame?** An open-source AI coding workflow toolkit that gives AI agents a repeatable delivery lifecycle so teams plan, prove and ship with discipline instead of ad-hoc prompting.
- **Which AI tools does it support?** Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode. Claude hooks are plugin-managed, Codex keeps config.toml user-owned, and OpenCode inherits the global/default model by default.
- **Do ShipFrame skills appear in /skills?** Yes in Codex after `shipframe install --codex`; Claude uses `/shipframe:<skill>` commands such as `/shipframe:code-review`; OpenCode loads skills through its native skill tool.
- **Is it free?** Yes, it is open source under the MIT License.
- **Does it work with GitHub and GitLab?** Yes — Draft Pull Requests on GitHub (gh CLI) and Draft Merge Requests on GitLab (glab CLI); the provider is auto-detected from the origin remote.
- **Do I have to change my workflow?** No — it is designed around tickets, Git branches and pull/merge requests, and you adopt only the skills you want.
